The quiet garden

A garden offers a quiet place to observe the changing seasons. Every morning, the light reaches a different corner of the stone wall, revealing small plants that were hidden in yesterday's shade. Patient observation is the beginning of understanding this living landscape.

Learning to look

There is no hurry when learning the names of familiar plants. A notebook and a little curiosity are enough. The field guide offers practical advice for anyone starting their own observations, including simple techniques for recording details.

  • Watch the morning light and record the weather.
  • Leave room for wildlife and native flowers.
A garden is a conversation with the seasons, and listening is as important as planting.

Returning to the same place throughout the year makes its patterns easier to recognise. Each visit adds another piece to a story that never quite finishes. The rewards are small and frequent, from the first spring shoot to the last leaf falling from a tree.
